## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** |

The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS.

## Modifications

- Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**.
- The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change.
- Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check.
- The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layout and values; short sequences keep the zero-copy view; long sequences are dense only on HIP; the copy preserves every bit (`torch.equal` against the transposed view).
- End to end, the change only moves tensor layout, so no numerical change is expected by construction. Verified on Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 and 2048^2 with a fixed seed: identical image, no metric shift.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1, default environment, `torch_sdpa` backend, gfx1151. Seconds per denoising step (mean over all steps), two runs per arm:

| Shape | before | after | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024^2 / 20 steps | 3.8524 | 3.8523 | 1.00x |
| 2048^2 / 12 steps | 78.04 / 77.42 | 22.04 / 22.11 | **3.54x** |

Within-arm spread <1%. The 2048^2 gain is AOTriton flash instead of the generic kernel; the 1024^2 row confirms the threshold leaves short sequences untouched.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit (`isort` + `ruff` pass).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations (no user-facing docs describe this backend detail).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

<!-- pr-check-comment runs=39964389849 -->
Required checks failed on e0ddf5b; this PR cannot be merged until they pass.

**Lint** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39964389849))
Run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and push the result. The run log shows any other failing step.

Lint is fixed in cd83cbaa3 — the pre-commit formatter wanted the platform-guard assert on a single line. Could a maintainer add the `run-ci` label so the AMD build and multimodal-gen unit tests can run? The docs preview also still needs "Approve preview" from someone with write access.

I ran a same-process A/B on RDNA4 (gfx1201) of SDPA on the strided heads-first view vs. dense copies (copy cost included, as in this PR). bf16, D=128, B=1, non-causal, `rocm/pytorch` ROCm 7.2.3 / torch 2.10. The arms are interleaved, 5 rounds, median time.

| H | S | strided (ms) | dense incl. copy (ms) | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 8192 | 8.24 | 8.59 | 0.96x |
| 12 | 32768 | 131.6 | 132.3 | 0.99x |
| 24 | 16384 | 65.3 | 66.5 | 0.98x |
| 24 | 32768 | 260.2 | 265.3 | 0.98x |
| 32 | 8192 | 22.4 | 23.3 | 0.96x |
| 32 | 10240 | 60.0 | 35.3 | 1.70x |
| 32 | 16384 | 299.0 | 88.1 | **3.39x** |
| 40 | 32768 | 433.5 | 442.8 | 0.98x |
| 48 | 16384 | 134.0 | 136.7 | 0.98x |
| 64 | 8192 | 194.4 | 47.9 | **4.06x** |
| 64 | 16384 | 1360.7 | 178.5 | **7.62x** |
| 96 | 8192 | 91.7 | 70.1 | 1.31x |

On this GPU, the cliff depends on the head count rather than on S alone. It shows up when the token stride of the heads-first view, H*D*2 bytes, is 8 KiB (H=32) or 16 KiB (H=64), and somewhat at 24 KiB (H=96). With H=12/16/24/40/48 the strided view stays on the fast path all the way to S=32768, and the copy costs 1-7% at S >= 8192.

With the current gate (HIP and S >= 8192), shapes like Wan2.1-1.3B (12 heads), FLUX / Qwen-Image (24 heads) and Wan2.1-14B (40 heads) would pay that small cost on gfx1201 with no gain. Meanwhile, H=64 already falls off the cliff at S=8192.

Your gfx1151 numbers are for 32 heads, so they are consistent with this. Would it make sense to also key the gate on the stride, for example `(H * D) % 4096 == 0`? Or does gfx1151 show the cliff for other head counts too?

For reference, #46515's Triton kernel on the same shapes is in a comment there.

Follow-up with RDNA3 (gfx1100, W7900-class) numbers. Same script and settings as above (bf16, D=128, B=1, non-causal, arms interleaved, median of 5 rounds), on torch 2.13 / ROCm 7.2:

| H | S | strided (ms) | dense incl. copy (ms) | gain | #46515 kernel (ms) | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 8192 | 6.71 | 7.44 | 0.90x | 7.22 | 0.93x |
| 12 | 32768 | 106.5 | 109.0 | 0.98x | 105.0 | 1.01x |
| 24 | 4096 | 3.49 | 4.40 | 0.79x | 4.24 | 0.82x |
| 24 | 16384 | 124.7 | 62.3 | **2.00x** | 57.8 | 2.16x |
| 32 | 8192 | 17.8 | 20.4 | 0.88x | 19.7 | 0.91x |
| 32 | 10240 | 28.0 | 31.0 | 0.90x | 29.9 | 0.94x |
| 32 | 16384 | 227.8 | 81.2 | **2.81x** | 75.1 | 3.03x |
| 40 | 16384 | 164.9 | 100.0 | **1.65x** | 93.2 | 1.77x |
| 48 | 16384 | 255.1 | 124.3 | **2.05x** | 115.6 | 2.21x |
| 64 | 8192 | 35.7 | 41.2 | 0.87x | 39.8 | 0.90x |

So the cliff is arch-dependent:
- **gfx1100:** every head count from 24 up falls off by S=16384, while nothing does at S <= 10240. There, the copy costs 7-12% (H=12 never falls off up to S=32768).
- **gfx1201:** only 32 and 64 heads fall off (see my earlier comment).
- **gfx1151:** your numbers show 32 heads at S=8192.

With a single `S >= 8192` gate, gfx1100 pays ~10% on S in [8192, 16384) and gets the large wins from 16384 on. A per-arch threshold, or one keyed on the measured shape, would avoid the loss on both RDNA cards.

For #46515: on gfx1100 its kernel is roughly on par with AOTriton on the strided view (0.82-1.01x) wherever SDPA has not fallen off. So the RDNA4 gain I reported does not carry over to RDNA3.

Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`4709a3a24e`) and re-verified on gfx1151.

**Rebase / checks.** The only conflict was the import block in `sdpa.py` (upstream added `get_forward_context_or_none`); resolved by keeping both imports. `ruff format`, `ruff --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037`, `isort`, and the new `scripts/lint/check_indirect_imports.py` are clean on the two touched files. `test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` passes 4/4 on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, AOTriton 0.11.1).

**gfx1151 head sweep.** Your RDNA4 numbers prompted this. Same protocol as yours: same process, arms interleaved, copy cost inside the dense arm, bf16 / D=128 / B=1 / non-causal, `TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`, 7 rounds, median.

| H | stride H·D·2 (B) | S=8192 | S=16384 | S=32768 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 3072 | 0.96× | 1.02× | 1.34× |
| 24 | 6144 | 1.02× | **2.07×** | **4.46×** |
| 32 | 8192 | **2.19×** | **6.82×** | **11.82×** |
| 40 | 10240 | 1.12× | **2.77×** | **4.75×** |
| 48 | 12288 | **2.88×** | **7.84×** | **12.58×** |
| 64 | 16384 | **2.80×** | **8.39×** | **12.31×** |

Gain = strided / dense including the copy. For scale, dense kernel-only at H=32 is 61.1 / 246.0 / 969.6 ms at S = 8192 / 16384 / 32768 versus 173.3 / 1937.2 / 12331.6 ms strided; the three copies themselves cost 0.5–12% of the strided arm.

So yes, gfx1151 falls off for other head counts as well, and the set matches neither RDNA card:

- 24, 32, 40, 48 and 64 all fall off by S=16384 (2.07–8.39×);
- 32, 48 and 64 already fall off at S=8192 (2.19–2.88×);
- only H=12 (stride 3072 B) stays on the fast path up to S=32768, where materializing is still a 1.34× win.

**On `(H * D) % 4096 == 0`.** Measured, that predicate does not describe gfx1151 and would give up real gains here. H=48 has H·D = 6144 — not a multiple — yet wins 2.88/7.84/12.58× at the three sizes; H=24 (H·D = 3072) is 2.07× at 16384; H=40 (H·D = 5120) 2.77×. The predicate would switch all three off. It does match H=32 and H=64, which fall off, so it reads as a gfx1201 property rather than a portable one.

**Suggested gate.** Keep HIP + `S >= 8192`. Across the 18 shapes above it is neutral-or-better in 17; the single loss is H=12 at S=8192 (0.96×, i.e. 4%), and H=12 recovers 1.34× by 32768. Finer gating would have to be per architecture — your gfx1100 rows fall off from H=24 at 16384, your gfx1201 rows from H=32/64, gfx1151 (this sweep) from H=32/48/64 at 8192 and H=24/40 at 16384 — and a stride predicate fitted to one card excludes gains on the other two. I'd rather keep the conservative gate than hard-code a table we cannot cross-check on gfx1100/gfx1201.

Happy to fold a per-arch predicate into this PR if maintainers prefer that; otherwise it is ready for the AMD lane (still needs the `run-ci` label).

Thanks for the gfx1151 sweep. Agreed, drop the `(H * D) % 4096 == 0` idea: it was fitted to gfx1201, and it doesn't hold on gfx1100 either (H=24/40/48 fall off there at S=16384, see my gfx1100 table above).

For reference, here is what the plain `S >= 8192` gate costs in my earlier runs on shapes where SDPA does not fall off: 0.87-0.90x on gfx1100 for S in [8192, 16384), and 0.96-0.99x on gfx1201 for the head counts that never fall off. That's small next to the 1.6-12x wins on the shapes that do.

@@ -20,7 +20,10 @@
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.forward_context import (
     get_forward_context_or_none,
 )
-from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import AttentionBackendEnum
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import (
+    AttentionBackendEnum,
+    current_platform,
+)
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
 from sglang.srt.model_executor.runner_backend_utils.breakable_cuda_graph import (
     is_in_breakable_cuda_graph,
@@ -71,6 +74,22 @@ def get_impl_cls() -> type["SDPAImpl"]:
     #     return FlashAttentionMetadata
 
 
+# AOTriton's flash path only applies to dense operands; on a strided
+# [B, H, S, D] view it falls back to a generic kernel. The heads-first view of
+# a contiguous [B, S, H, D] activation is always strided, so the copy decides
+# between the two. Measured on gfx1151 (32 heads x 128, bf16):
+#
+#     S      1024   2048   4096   8192  16384
+#     gain   1.18x  1.09x  1.30x  3.01x  9.28x
+#
+# Below the threshold the copy buys little and the allocation churn costs more
+# than it saves: Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) lost 5.7% end to end while
+# its attention kernel alone was 1.3x faster, whereas at 2048^2 (S=16384) the
+# step time dropped 3.5x. So materialize only where the kernel gain dominates.
+_DENSE_SDPA_OPERANDS = current_platform.is_hip()
+_DENSE_SDPA_MIN_SEQ = 8192
+
+
 class SDPAImpl(AttentionImpl):
     def __init__(
         self,
@@ -100,9 +119,7 @@ def forward(
         attn_metadata: AttentionMetadata,
     ) -> torch.Tensor:
         # transpose to bs, heads, seq_len, head_dim
-        query = query.transpose(1, 2)
-        key = key.transpose(1, 2)
-        value = value.transpose(1, 2)
+        query, key, value = sdpa_operands(query, key, value)
         attn_mask = None
         is_causal = self.causal
         if self.causal and query.shape[-2] != key.shape[-2]:
@@ -403,3 +420,15 @@ def forward(
                 )
                 self._cudnn_failed = True
         return self.fa_impl.forward(query, key, value, attn_metadata, **kwargs)
+
+
+def sdpa_operands(query, key, value):
+    """[B, S, H, D] activations -> the [B, H, S, D] SDPA takes, dense when it pays."""
+    query, key, value = (
+        query.transpose(1, 2),
+        key.transpose(1, 2),
+        value.transpose(1, 2),
+    )
+    if not _DENSE_SDPA_OPERANDS or query.shape[-2] < _DENSE_SDPA_MIN_SEQ:
+        return query, key, value
+    return query.contiguous(), key.contiguous(), value.contiguous()

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Layout, values and the length gate of the SDPA operand helper.
+
+``scaled_dot_product_attention`` takes ``[B, H, S, D]``. The heads-first view of
+a ``[B, S, H, D]`` activation is strided, and AOTriton's flash path only applies
+to dense operands, so on HIP the backend materializes the view - but only for
+sequences long enough that the kernel gain outweighs the copy.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends import sdpa as sdpa_backend
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms import current_platform
+
+_SHAPE = (2, 5, 3, 8)  # [B, S, H, D]
+_LONG_SEQ = sdpa_backend._DENSE_SDPA_MIN_SEQ
+_LONG_SHAPE = (1, _LONG_SEQ, 2, 8)
+
+
+def _activations(shape=_SHAPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    return tuple(torch.randn(shape, dtype=dtype) for _ in range(3))
+
+
+class TestSDPAOperandLayout(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_layout_is_heads_first(self):
+        query, key, value = _activations()
+        out = sdpa_backend.sdpa_operands(query, key, value)
+        for src, got in zip((query, key, value), out):
+            self.assertEqual(got.shape, (2, 3, 5, 8))
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got, src.transpose(1, 2)))
+
+    def test_short_sequences_keep_the_view(self):
+        query, key, value = _activations()
+        got = sdpa_backend.sdpa_operands(query, key, value)
+        # Below the threshold no memory is spent, whatever the platform.
+        for out, src in zip(got, (query, key, value)):
+            self.assertEqual(
+                out.untyped_storage().data_ptr(), src.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+            )
+
+    def test_long_sequences_are_dense_on_hip(self):
+        query, key, value = _activations(_LONG_SHAPE)
+        got = sdpa_backend.sdpa_operands(query, key, value)
+        materialized = sdpa_backend._DENSE_SDPA_OPERANDS
+        for out, src in zip(got, (query, key, value)):
+            self.assertEqual(out.is_contiguous(), materialized)
+            # The copy is layout-only: values stay bit-identical either way.
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out, src.transpose(1, 2)))
+
+    def test_guard_matches_the_platform(self):
+        self.assertEqual(sdpa_backend._DENSE_SDPA_OPERANDS, current_platform.is_hip())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

So the cliff is arch-dependent:
- **gfx1100:** every head count from 24 up falls off by S=16384, while nothing does at S <= 10240. There, the copy costs 7-12% (H=12 never falls off up to S=32768).
- **gfx1201:** only 32 and 64 heads fall off (see my earlier comment).
- **gfx1151:** your numbers show 32 heads at S=8192.

With a single `S >= 8192` gate, gfx1100 pays ~10% on S in [8192, 16384) and gets the large wins from 16384 on. A per-arch threshold, or one keyed on the measured shape, would avoid the loss on both RDNA cards.

**gfx1151 head sweep.** Your RDNA4 numbers prompted this. Same protocol as yours: same process, arms interleaved, copy cost inside the dense arm, bf16 / D=128 / B=1 / non-causal, `TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`, 7 rounds, median.

| H | stride H·D·2 (B) | S=8192 | S=16384 | S=32768 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 3072 | 0.96× | 1.02× | 1.34× |
| 24 | 6144 | 1.02× | **2.07×** | **4.46×** |
| 32 | 8192 | **2.19×** | **6.82×** | **11.82×** |
| 40 | 10240 | 1.12× | **2.77×** | **4.75×** |
| 48 | 12288 | **2.88×** | **7.84×** | **12.58×** |
| 64 | 16384 | **2.80×** | **8.39×** | **12.31×** |

Gain = strided / dense including the copy. For scale, dense kernel-only at H=32 is 61.1 / 246.0 / 969.6 ms at S = 8192 / 16384 / 32768 versus 173.3 / 1937.2 / 12331.6 ms strided; the three copies themselves cost 0.5–12% of the strided arm.

So yes, gfx1151 falls off for other head counts as well, and the set matches neither RDNA card:

- 24, 32, 40, 48 and 64 all fall off by S=16384 (2.07–8.39×);
- 32, 48 and 64 already fall off at S=8192 (2.19–2.88×);
- only H=12 (stride 3072 B) stays on the fast path up to S=32768, where materializing is still a 1.34× win.

**On `(H * D) % 4096 == 0`.** Measured, that predicate does not describe gfx1151 and would give up real gains here. H=48 has H·D = 6144 — not a multiple — yet wins 2.88/7.84/12.58× at the three sizes; H=24 (H·D = 3072) is 2.07× at 16384; H=40 (H·D = 5120) 2.77×. The predicate would switch all three off. It does match H=32 and H=64, which fall off, so it reads as a gfx1201 property rather than a portable one.

**Suggested gate.** Keep HIP + `S >= 8192`. Across the 18 shapes above it is neutral-or-better in 17; the single loss is H=12 at S=8192 (0.96×, i.e. 4%), and H=12 recovers 1.34× by 32768. Finer gating would have to be per architecture — your gfx1100 rows fall off from H=24 at 16384, your gfx1201 rows from H=32/64, gfx1151 (this sweep) from H=32/48/64 at 8192 and H=24/40 at 16384 — and a stride predicate fitted to one card excludes gains on the other two. I'd rather keep the conservative gate than hard-code a table we cannot cross-check on gfx1100/gfx1201.

Happy to fold a per-arch predicate into this PR if maintainers prefer that; otherwise it is ready for the AMD lane (still needs the `run-ci` label).
